coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional matched blood measurement, 100 modified cells fall to five after a trigger, a 95 per cent reduction. A cytokine readout falls, but organ injury is unchanged. These are three different outcomes: sampled cell abundance, inflammatory signal and injury. Ask whether viable survivors retain receptor function, which tissues were sampled, when the measurements were made and whether survivors regrow. A sequence check or six people observed for four weeks without an event cannot establish a functioning rescue mechanism, complete body-wide clearance, zero risk or reversal of an injury already present. A usable control plan also depends on switch expression, trigger delivery to the relevant cells and access to the drug and specialist care; an encoded switch alone establishes none of these.

In mouse adoptive-transfer experiments, a nonmyeloablative regimen enhanced antitumour effect even without regulatory T cells, through greater function of tumour-reactive CD8-positive T cells rather than greater numbers; interleukin-7 and interleukin-15 were required, and removing endogenous cells that respond to those cytokines reproduced the effect, which points to lymphodepletion removing cells that act as cytokine sinks (Gattinoni et al.). That is a mouse mechanism and it does not describe an empty physical space. When a trial tests conditioning, transferred cells and cytokine support together, the outcomes belong to the whole package: in the phase 3 tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte trial in advanced melanoma (Rohaan et al.; 168 patients, 86 per cent with disease refractory to anti-PD-1 treatment), cells were infused after nonmyeloablative cyclophosphamide plus fludarabine and followed by high-dose interleukin-2, and grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in all patients given TILs, mainly chemotherapy-related myelosuppression. Nonmyeloablative therefore does not mean harmless.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Counts need their denominators. A percentage of white cells is not an absolute count: with invented numbers, 20 per cent of 2,000 white cells per microlitre is 400 lymphocytes, and a later 40 per cent of 500 is 200, so the fraction doubled while the count halved. Lymphocyte and neutrophil counts are separate measurements, cytopenia means a low count of any blood cell type, and none of these measures tumour killing.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Lymphocytes include T cells, B cells and natural killer cells. Preparation can affect competition, regulation and, for donor products, host rejection; it can also act on cancer directly. It does not create a missing tumour antigen or guarantee that transferred cells enter a solid tumour. The need for preparation and its recovery criteria belong to the named protocol, rather than to every cell therapy. Serial blood counts consume blood samples rather than tumour tissue. Report absolute lymphocytes and neutrophils with units, sampling time and reference ranges, and measure transferred-cell number, location and function separately from the counts. More depletion is not automatically more benefit. Nonmyeloablative describes a regimen not intended to eliminate marrow blood production completely, rather than a promise of mild count suppression. Report severity, duration, recovery, infections, organ harms and relevant support with the regimen. More transferred cells, more depletion and more tumour killing are separate propositions.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A cell-therapy recognition claim needs the actual binder and accessible epitope, including tumour cells that lack it and relevant healthy cells. Sun’s TROP2 CAR used a sacituzumab-derived binding fragment. Human-cell and TNBC xenograft experiments tested antitumour activity; a separate murine-cell construct in mice expressing human TROP2 tested toxicity. The ungated construct caused lung injury and inflammation in that model. This does not turn an RNA measurement, an antibody stain or an antibody-drug conjugate result into a demonstration of safe human CAR-T recognition. Expression can vary within and between lesions and after treatment. Bulk RNA, soluble protein and an antibody stain need not report the feature accessible to the finished receptor.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional population of 100 cancer cells, 80 display target X and 20 do not. Killing the X-positive 80 leaves 20 survivors; ten times as many effector cells does not create X on them. For two targets, suppose 20 cells carry both X and Y, 60 carry X only, ten Y only and ten neither. An idealised either-target rule covers 90 cells, whereas a both-target rule covers 20. These are recognition-coverage calculations, not measured killing or healthy-tissue selectivity. Expression thresholds, tissue access and cell function still matter.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Two primary reports show the contrast. A patient with colon cancer metastatic to the lungs and liver received 10 billion autologous T cells expressing a trastuzumab-based CAR against ERBB2 (HER2), the largest number permitted in the first dose-escalation cohort, the day after a lymphodepleting regimen of cyclophosphamide (60 mg/kg daily for 2 days) and fludarabine (25 mg/m2 for 5 days). Within 15 minutes the patient had respiratory distress, chest imaging showed pulmonary oedema, and the patient died 5 days after treatment, with marked rises in interferon-gamma, GM-CSF, tumour necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-6 and interleukin-10. At autopsy multiple organs showed systemic ischaemia and haemorrhagic microangiopathic injury and the lungs diffuse alveolar damage; histological examination of autopsy tissue found ERBB2 at 3+ in liver metastases and 2+ in lung metastases and much lower levels in normal lung parenchyma, normal liver and normal breast. The authors hypothesised that highly active ERBB2-directed T cells recognised ERBB2 on normal lung cells on first pass through the lung and released inflammatory cytokines that began a cascade ending in multiorgan failure; the autopsy findings were read as initial lung injury followed by days of hypotension and ischaemia, and the authors call the significance of the cells' reactivity against cultured primary cells unclear. This is a single case, with a stated dose and conditioning, whose mechanism is the authors' hypothesis and which gives no incidence for any CAR product (Morgan et al., 2010). In a trial of an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor against HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3 in myeloma and melanoma, the first two patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days; no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and beating cardiomyocytes made from induced pluripotent stem cells triggered T-cell killing through recognition of an unrelated peptide from titin. That is off-target recognition of an unintended molecule, not the intended target in the wrong tissue (Linette et al., 2013).

FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Suppose two fictional CARs differ only in their hinge: both bind purified antigen, but only one kills antigen-bearing cells. Compare surface expression and the geometry of cell contact before concluding that affinity is the problem. Likewise, DNA-positive cells without killing leave RNA production, receptor folding and trafficking, actual binding and signalling as separate possible failure points. Hudecek’s R11 ROR1 experiments illustrate a product-specific constraint: a long spacer enabled recognition of its membrane-proximal epitope, while changes that reduced Fc-receptor binding improved activity in the tested mice. Longer is not a universal design rule. Treat the transmembrane segment as part of the finished construct: assess assembly, surface expression and interactions rather than presume it is a neutral anchor. Unstimulated signalling and responses to repeated target encounters also need separate assessment.

The receptor recognizes a displayed peptide-HLA complex, rather than entering the tumor cell to bind the whole source protein. Natural processing, the required HLA allele, surface display, receptor expression and useful cell function remain different questions. This differs from administering a soluble TCR/CD3 protein that recruits other T cells.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cells respond biologically to signals, without intention; more cells do not by themselves establish better or safer treatment. Consider two fictional ready-made products: a carrier that gives receptor instructions to the recipient’s own T cells, and a prepared batch of donor-derived engineered cells. The first can generate autologous cells in vivo; the second supplies allogeneic cells engineered ex vivo. State four things separately: the starting cell family, whose cells they are, where engineering happens and whether cells or an instruction carrier are administered. Neither card establishes available supply, the final engineered-cell population or treatment benefit. NK and NKT name different cell families; an added receptor does not erase the recipient cell’s other inputs.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Each connected action adds its own requirement. For an antibody-drug conjugate, FDA's March 2024 clinical pharmacology guidance defines total antibody, unconjugated antibody and unconjugated payload as separate quantities and says its principles may not apply to other types of conjugate. A T-cell engager needs productive contact between two cells, a receptor needs a relevant effect on signalling, and a CAR needs surface expression and target-dependent activation, which Eshhar et al. (1993) first showed in a T-cell hybridoma. Delivery binders choose the cell that receives instructions (Rurik et al., 2022), which can differ from the cancer cell. Attaching a binder shows none of these later steps.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Definitions. A conventional antibody pairs heavy- and light-chain variable domains to form a binding site. A single-chain variable fragment (scFv) joins those two domains with a peptide linker in one polypeptide chain, so single-chain does not mean one variable domain (Huston et al., 1988, a 15-amino-acid linker). VHH is the binding domain of a camelid heavy-chain-only antibody (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993), and an isolated VHH used as a binder is called a nanobody (Bathula et al., 2021). Not every engineered single-domain antibody derives from a camelid VHH, a point the source lesson makes without a primary citation in this batch.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Format changes what is tested. A soluble molecule must stay intact and usable through manufacture, storage and exposure, and adding binding units or a chemical cargo can change its behaviour (Junutula et al., 2008, anti-MUC16 conjugate in mice, rats and monkeys). A CAR fixes the binder to a membrane and links contact to signalling, so spacer reach, target position, expression and clustering matter (Hudecek et al., 2015; Long et al., 2015). The same recognition sequence therefore does not guarantee the same performance.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Kawalekar’s defined human-CAR experiments linked 4-1BB signalling to outgrowth of CD8 central-memory cells with greater respiratory capacity, fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis. CD28-containing CARs produced effector-memory cells with a gene-expression pattern consistent with greater glycolysis. These are construct-and-system observations, not a ranking of clinical speed, persistence or safety by domain name. Other receptor parts, preparation, starting-cell state, target and disease setting remain relevant. Ramos simultaneously infused separately tracked second- and third-generation products. Their different expansion and persistence did not let a shared tumour response isolate either product’s clinical contribution.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Suppose two fictional CARs differ only in their hinge: both bind purified antigen, but only one kills antigen-bearing cells. Likewise, DNA-positive cells without killing leave RNA production, receptor folding and trafficking, actual binding and signalling as separate possible failure points. Unstimulated signalling and responses to repeated target encounters also need separate assessment.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Where the DNA sits was measured in different systems. In sequential muscle biopsies taken 3 and 12 months after an intramuscular AAV vector expressing alpha-1 antitrypsin, most vector DNA was double-stranded circular episomes, and clones recovered from the biopsies were transcriptionally active (Schnepp and colleagues; abstract read, full text not retrievable). After partial hepatectomy in mice, extrachromosomal genomes were the main form behind liver expression and in most cases no more than about 10 per cent of stably transduced genomes had integrated, although one of three mice at a higher dose had 67 per cent integrated genomes (Nakai and colleagues). coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cytokines are signalling proteins whose binding to a suitable receptor changes signalling and gene expression in a receiving cell. Autocrine action is on the producing cell, paracrine action is on neighbours, and endocrine action is at a distance, for example after entry into the circulation. Distant action is possible rather than the default for every cytokine (British Society for Immunology, Cytokines: Introduction). Chemokines are a cytokine family involved in cell recruitment and can also affect leukocyte activation (NLM MeSH, Chemokines). The information-versus-fuel distinction is a reading rule: a measured amount of signalling protein does not measure the energy available to the cell, and a message without the relevant receptor and response machinery does not establish a response.

The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional population of 100 cancer cells, 80 display target X and 20 do not. Killing the X-positive 80 leaves 20 survivors; ten times as many effector cells does not create X on them. For two targets, suppose 20 cells carry both X and Y, 60 carry X only, ten Y only and ten neither. An idealised either-target rule covers 90 cells, whereas a both-target rule covers 20. These are recognition-coverage calculations, not measured killing or healthy-tissue selectivity. Expression thresholds, tissue access and cell function still matter.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional target cell, HLA allele A is lost while B remains. An A-restricted receptor loses that route; a B-restricted receptor still needs its own peptide to be processed and displayed. B2M is the shared light chain for many class-I complexes, whereas class-II HLA uses different alpha and beta chains. Neither one lost allele nor a change in interferon-induced display establishes complete loss of baseline presentation. Test the required allele, antigen and display conditions with matched viable targets rather than infer recognition from the HLA label. A conventional surface-antigen CAR has another dependency, and reduced class I alone does not guarantee NK-cell killing.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The tumour microenvironment includes neighbouring cells, extracellular material, vessels and local physical conditions. A neighbouring cell need not belong to the malignant clone. Cell populations, cytokines and chemokines, matrix, oxygen, nutrients and waste interact in both directions, and their arrangement varies between regions, disease sites and times. A drawing is a map of possible participants, not a measured recipe or a fixed job description.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The adenosine route works outside cells. CD39 (ENTPD1) and CD73 (NT5E) are enzymes that help generate adenosine from extracellular ATP and ADP, and adenosine then acts on cell-surface receptors, including the A2A receptor on T cells. The enzymes can sit on immune cells, cancer cells or other tissue cells, so the source has to be measured and not assumed. The IDO route works inside a producing cell: IDO1 starts the breakdown of tryptophan along the kynurenine pathway. IDO is not an adenosine receptor and does not degrade ATP, so the two routes should not be merged into one 'suppressive axis'.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: How the question is asked before and during trials. FDA's CAR T-cell development guidance says to assess both undesired targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target/off-tumour) and unintended targeting of other antigens, using examples such as tissue cross-reactivity studies with an antibody carrying the same recognition domain, protein arrays, cytotoxicity and cytokine-release testing on panels of primary cells, cell lines or stem-cell-derived organ systems, and relevant animal models, and encourages a combination of methods; antigen recognition domains can differ in affinity or avidity or recognise a different site, which should be evaluated, and CAR T cells can carry added components such as suicide genes. In practice a readout is a staining intensity or positive fraction, a binding profile, killing or cytokine release by healthy cells at a named time, and finally organ injury in the treated population; stained fixed tissue does not show a living organ's accessibility, an animal model may lack the human target, and a negative result in one panel is not a safety certificate. No universal expression cut-off is given here because no source read gives one. Whether affinity tuning, recognition logic or control switches improve safety for a particular design needs that design's own evidence. The 2026 ASTCT consensus abstract lists on-target, off-tumour toxicity among the toxicities for which it considered definitions and grading; its criteria were not readable.

Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

The 2019 ASTCT consensus defines and grades CRS using attributed clinical findings, including fever at onset and the blood-pressure or oxygen support required. Its scale is a reporting framework, not a management algorithm. The 2026 ASTCT consensus expands the toxicity framework, but its detailed criteria were not accessible for this entry; the numerical grading below is explicitly the 2019 version. Product, disease, preparation, observation window and treated denominator must accompany any incidence estimate.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional matched blood measurement, 100 modified cells fall to five after a trigger, a 95 per cent reduction. A cytokine readout falls, but organ injury is unchanged. These are three different outcomes: sampled cell abundance, inflammatory signal and injury. coverageEvidence.excerpt: This historical single-arm phase-I dose-escalation report, within a phase-I/II programme, used a 9 September 2022 cutoff. Gavo-cel comprised autologous T cells engineered ex vivo with an antibody-CD3-epsilon fusion recognising surface mesothelin without a conventional peptide-HLA requirement. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.
coverageEvidence.sourceScope: FDA-LTFU-2020: nonbinding regulator guidance, Targeted integration, genome-editing and delayed-risk background paragraphs; not the whole document

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional follow-up example, an engineered-cell clone becomes more common but no new malignancy has been established. The observation prompts examination of the clone, insertion sites, gene effects and clinical findings. A growth pattern, a malignant diagnosis and an insertion-driven mechanism are separate claims. An insertion that leaves no demonstrated gene effect, one that interrupts a gene and one that alters nearby regulation are different possibilities; none of those schematic locations assigns an incidence or time to cancer. A CAR-positive malignancy can establish product ancestry without identifying which change drove it.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A transposon system has two parts: a cargo cassette flanked by boundary sequences, and a transposase that recognises those boundaries and catalyses insertion. The transposase can be supplied as protein or through instructions that make it, and the cell has to receive both in usable form; the system does not itself deliver anything. Sleeping Beauty was reconstructed from inactive fish elements, and its transposase bound the inverted repeats and mediated precise cut-and-paste transposition in fish, mouse and human cells (Ivics and colleagues).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Three primary reports show why the setting matters. After retrovirus-mediated gamma-c gene transfer into autologous CD34-positive bone marrow cells for X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency, 9 of 10 patients were corrected, but almost three years later the two youngest developed uncontrolled clonal proliferation of mature T cells; both clones carried vector integration near the LMO2 proto-oncogene promoter with abnormal LMO2 expression, which the authors attributed most likely to retrovirus enhancer activity (Hacein-Bey-Abina et al., 2003). In a patient with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia given CD19 CAR T cells, 94 per cent of CAR T cells at the peak of response came from one clone in which lentiviral insertion had disrupted TET2, the patient's second TET2 allele carried a hypomorphic mutation, and the clone showed a central memory phenotype alongside complete remission: an expanded clone linked to benefit, not a new cancer (Fraietta et al., 2018). In 724 patients treated with T-cell therapies at one centre, a lethal T-cell lymphoma followed axicabtagene ciloleucel for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; the tumour, the CAR T cells and the patient's normal blood cells were profiled in depth, both lymphomas were Epstein-Barr virus positive and linked to DNMT3A and TET2 mutant clonal haematopoiesis, and no evidence of oncogenic retroviral integration was found with multiple techniques (Hamilton et al., 2024). The first is a specific stem-cell regimen and the others are single-centre or single-patient observations, so none is an incidence estimate for a vector or product.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: What regulators ask for follows from this. The August 2026 ABECMA prescribing information carries a boxed warning that T-cell malignancies, including CAR-positive tumours, have occurred after BCMA- and CD19-directed genetically modified autologous T-cell immunotherapies for blood cancers, may present within weeks of infusion and may be fatal, and says to monitor life-long for secondary malignancies. coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

CAR-positive T cells are 50/100, or 50 per cent of T cells, but T cells are 50/200, or 25 per cent of all CAR-positive cells. coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: This historical single-arm phase-I dose-escalation report, within a phase-I/II programme, used a 9 September 2022 cutoff. Gavo-cel comprised autologous T cells engineered ex vivo with an antibody-CD3-epsilon fusion recognising surface mesothelin without a conventional peptide-HLA requirement. The treated cancers were mesothelioma, ovarian cancer and cholangiocarcinoma. Forty-eight people underwent apheresis intending phase-I infusion, 32 were treated and 30 were response-evaluable. Two grade-5 adverse events occurred before post-infusion imaging. Blinded independent central review found six responses, four confirmed partial responses: 6/30 is 20 per cent, 6/48 is 12.5 per cent and 4/30 is about 13.3 per cent, reported as 13 per cent. Each fraction needs its analysis population, reviewer, rule and confirmation status. Missing scans do not settle safety or causal attribution, and this study does not estimate comparative benefit in another cancer. Response confirmation, response duration, survival and quality of life are different outcomes. The historical cutoff and a source-check date do not establish current recruitment, approval, availability or personal eligibility.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Among the 32 treated participants, 25 had cytokine release syndrome: 17 grade 1 or 2, six grade 3 and two grade 4. One person had brief, self-limited ICANS. The report used the 2019 ASTCT framework for those syndromes and CTCAE version 5 for other adverse events. Tocilizumab was given to 17 participants with CRS, including 11 also given corticosteroids; eight did not require anti-cytokine treatment. Everyone infused had at least 12 weeks of safety follow-up. Median CRS onset was three days (range zero to nine), and median duration was six days (range one to 55). These are observations under the report’s rules, not a bedside treatment algorithm, an explanation of each clinician’s decision or a randomised estimate that an intervention caused recovery.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cells respond biologically to signals, without intention; more cells do not by themselves establish better or safer treatment. Consider two fictional ready-made products: a carrier that gives receptor instructions to the recipient’s own T cells, and a prepared batch of donor-derived engineered cells. The first can generate autologous cells in vivo; the second supplies allogeneic cells engineered ex vivo. State four things separately: the starting cell family, whose cells they are, where engineering happens and whether cells or an instruction carrier are administered. Neither card establishes available supply, the final engineered-cell population or treatment benefit. NK and NKT name different cell families; an added receptor does not erase the recipient cell’s other inputs.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional tumour sample, 70 of 100 cells display an epitope accessible to the proposed receptor and 30 do not. A second target has only an RNA result, while healthy tissue was stained with a third antibody. Those measurements cannot rank safe receptor designs: ask for the actual binder’s recognition, the unrecognised tumour population and functional effects on relevant healthy cells. A more sensitive receptor might recognise additional tumour cells and additional healthy cells. Even a perfectly specific binder can harm healthy cells carrying its intended antigen; unintended binding to another molecule is a different failure. A sampled panel can miss antigen-negative cells, and an intracellular signal does not establish an accessible surface epitope. Repeat the relevant healthy-cell question under conditions, including inflammation, that could change recognition.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

In vivo engineering administers an instruction-carrying product and generates modified cells inside the body; it is not the same as testing an ex vivo product in an animal. coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Definitions. A conventional antibody pairs heavy- and light-chain variable domains to form a binding site. VHH is the binding domain of a camelid heavy-chain-only antibody (Hamers-Casterman et al., 1993), and an isolated VHH used as a binder is called a nanobody (Bathula et al., 2021). Not every engineered single-domain antibody derives from a camelid VHH, a point the source lesson makes without a primary citation in this batch.

These are properties of the soluble protein. A cell carrying a small binder does not penetrate tissue like a small soluble protein. A source lesson gives 25 to 27 kDa and 12 to 15 kDa, which differ from the ranges in the sources it cites.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cytokines are signalling proteins whose binding to a suitable receptor changes signalling and gene expression in a receiving cell. Distant action is possible rather than the default for every cytokine (British Society for Immunology, Cytokines: Introduction). Chemokines are a cytokine family involved in cell recruitment and can also affect leukocyte activation (NLM MeSH, Chemokines). The information-versus-fuel distinction is a reading rule: a measured amount of signalling protein does not measure the energy available to the cell, and a message without the relevant receptor and response machinery does not establish a response.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cells respond biologically to signals, without intention; more cells do not by themselves establish better or safer treatment. Consider two fictional ready-made products: a carrier that gives receptor instructions to the recipient’s own T cells, and a prepared batch of donor-derived engineered cells. The first can generate autologous cells in vivo; the second supplies allogeneic cells engineered ex vivo. State four things separately: the starting cell family, whose cells they are, where engineering happens and whether cells or an instruction carrier are administered. Neither card establishes available supply, the final engineered-cell population or treatment benefit. NK and NKT name different cell families; an added receptor does not erase the recipient cell’s other inputs.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A carrier delivers a genetic payload. Transduction is vector-mediated gene transfer; integration places DNA in a chromosome; expression produces an encoded RNA or protein. These are different events. Follow the causal chain in separate steps: administered carrier, distribution and cell contact, entry and usable cargo release, expression in identified cells, survival or expansion and movement, then recognition and effects in tumour and healthy tissue. Fluorescent uptake need not mean useful expression, and detecting two components somewhere in a sample does not show that the same cells express both. A carrier-lot aliquot, a timed blood sample and a tissue biopsy answer different questions. Sequence copies, viable receptor-positive fractions and controlled killing cannot substitute for one another or supply a universal release threshold. A carrier name does not determine its administration route. FDA’s CAR T-cell guidance focuses on ex vivo products; its principles do not by themselves validate a release specification for an in vivo carrier.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Three design labels are easy to confuse. Replication-defective means the delivered particle lacks the machinery to propagate as an ordinary virus, which does not replace testing: FDA guidance sets out testing of retroviral vector products, lentiviral ones included, for replication-competent virus during manufacture and in patient follow-up. Self-inactivating means regulatory sequences in the long terminal repeats are disabled: in the original design a 133 base-pair deletion in the U3 region of the 3' repeat was copied to the 5' repeat after reverse transcription and integration, and the vector still expressed from an internal promoter in rat brain and eye (Miyoshi and colleagues). It does not mean the cassette cannot integrate. Integration-deficient means integrase is mutated: with a class 1 integrase mutation, residual integration was lower than with intact integrase by a factor of 500 to 1,250, expression was transient in dividing cell lines and long-lived in non-dividing neural cultures and in mouse brain, consistent with an episomal genome (Philippe and colleagues). The name does not promise zero integration or lasting expression in dividing cells such as T cells.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Where the DNA sits was measured in different systems. In sequential muscle biopsies taken 3 and 12 months after an intramuscular AAV vector expressing alpha-1 antitrypsin, most vector DNA was double-stranded circular episomes, and clones recovered from the biopsies were transcriptionally active (Schnepp and colleagues; abstract read, full text not retrievable). After partial hepatectomy in mice, extrachromosomal genomes were the main form behind liver expression and in most cases no more than about 10 per cent of stably transduced genomes had integrated, although one of three mice at a higher dose had 67 per cent integrated genomes (Nakai and colleagues). That shows the usual behaviour of the tested vectors in those tissues, not that integration never happens, and persistent DNA does not show an intact cassette, enough protein or a surviving functional cell: in the muscle study the episomal inverted terminal repeats ranged from fully intact to severely deleted, so counting vector DNA is a different measurement from showing a working cassette.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A transposon system has two parts: a cargo cassette flanked by boundary sequences, and a transposase that recognises those boundaries and catalyses insertion. The transposase can be supplied as protein or through instructions that make it, and the cell has to receive both in usable form; the system does not itself deliver anything. Sleeping Beauty was reconstructed from inactive fish elements, and its transposase bound the inverted repeats and mediated precise cut-and-paste transposition in fish, mouse and human cells (Ivics and colleagues).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Lymphocytes include T cells, B cells and natural killer cells. Preparation can affect competition, regulation and, for donor products, host rejection; it can also act on cancer directly. It does not create a missing tumour antigen or guarantee that transferred cells enter a solid tumour. The need for preparation and its recovery criteria belong to the named protocol, rather than to every cell therapy. Serial blood counts consume blood samples rather than tumour tissue. Report absolute lymphocytes and neutrophils with units, sampling time and reference ranges, and measure transferred-cell number, location and function separately from the counts. More depletion is not automatically more benefit. Nonmyeloablative describes a regimen not intended to eliminate marrow blood production completely, rather than a promise of mild count suppression. Report severity, duration, recovery, infections, organ harms and relevant support with the regimen. More transferred cells, more depletion and more tumour killing are separate propositions.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

The 2019 ASTCT consensus defines and grades CRS using attributed clinical findings, including fever at onset and the blood-pressure or oxygen support required. Its scale is a reporting framework, not a management algorithm. The 2026 ASTCT consensus expands the toxicity framework, but its detailed criteria were not accessible for this entry; the numerical grading below is explicitly the 2019 version. Product, disease, preparation, observation window and treated denominator must accompany any incidence estimate.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, or ICANS, is a neurologic syndrome associated with immune-effector-cell therapy. Changes in language, attention, handwriting or awareness and more severe findings such as seizures need assessment against baseline and alternative explanations. An immune-marker plot does not establish the syndrome.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional matched blood measurement, 100 modified cells fall to five after a trigger, a 95 per cent reduction. A cytokine readout falls, but organ injury is unchanged. These are three different outcomes: sampled cell abundance, inflammatory signal and injury. Ask whether viable survivors retain receptor function, which tissues were sampled, when the measurements were made and whether survivors regrow. A sequence check or six people observed for four weeks without an event cannot establish a functioning rescue mechanism, complete body-wide clearance, zero risk or reversal of an injury already present. A usable control plan also depends on switch expression, trigger delivery to the relevant cells and access to the drug and specialist care; an encoded switch alone establishes none of these.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Cytokines are signalling proteins whose binding to a suitable receptor changes signalling and gene expression in a receiving cell. Autocrine action is on the producing cell, paracrine action is on neighbours, and endocrine action is at a distance, for example after entry into the circulation. Distant action is possible rather than the default for every cytokine (British Society for Immunology, Cytokines: Introduction). Chemokines are a cytokine family involved in cell recruitment and can also affect leukocyte activation (NLM MeSH, Chemokines). The information-versus-fuel distinction is a reading rule: a measured amount of signalling protein does not measure the energy available to the cell, and a message without the relevant receptor and response machinery does not establish a response.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a fictional target cell, HLA allele A is lost while B remains. An A-restricted receptor loses that route; a B-restricted receptor still needs its own peptide to be processed and displayed. B2M is the shared light chain for many class-I complexes, whereas class-II HLA uses different alpha and beta chains. Neither one lost allele nor a change in interferon-induced display establishes complete loss of baseline presentation. Test the required allele, antigen and display conditions with matched viable targets rather than infer recognition from the HLA label. A conventional surface-antigen CAR has another dependency, and reduced class I alone does not guarantee NK-cell killing.

coverageEvidence.excerpt:
Vein-to-vein time is the interval from collection of a person’s cells to infusion of the prepared cell product. Collection, transport, manufacture, testing, release and clinical readiness contribute to that interval; culture time alone does not describe it. The definition, starting event and analysis population should be stated when comparing programmes.

FDA’s 2024 CAR T-cell guidance recommends planning for manufacturing delays or failures, reassessing eligibility before administration and analysing failure to reach treatment as a possible feasibility endpoint. A product that does not meet its release criteria and a person who becomes unable to receive treatment are different events. Neither a generic turnaround estimate nor a cross-trial waiting-time difference by itself establishes why clinical outcomes differ.
